295.h: Madonna University is a private Catholic university founded by Very Reverend Father Professor Emmanuel Matthew Paul Edeh, a priest of the Holy Ghost Congregation. It began in the late 1990s, and the National Universities Commission records its establishment in 1999, among the first private universities licensed in Nigeria.
295.a: Madonna offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, with well-known faculties of medicine, pharmacy and law, within a Catholic ethos.
295.c: The main campus is at Okija in Anambra State. Students live on campus.

298.h: McPherson University (McU) is a private Christian university established in 2012 by the Foursquare Gospel Church in Nigeria. It is named after Aimee Semple McPherson, the American evangelist who founded the Foursquare Gospel Church.
298.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
298.c: The campus is at Seriki Sotayo in Ogun State, off the Lagos-Ibadan expressway.

299.h: Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike (MOUAU) is a federal university of agriculture. It was created as the Federal University of Agriculture, Umudike, by Federal Government Decree No. 48 of November 1992, and was later renamed after Michael Okpara, premier of the former Eastern Region. Its first council and its first vice-chancellor, Professor Placid C. Njoku, were appointed on 27 May 1993, and the first 82 students were admitted in the 1993/94 session.
299.a: MOUAU specialises in agriculture and allied fields such as animal science, crop and soil science, food science, veterinary medicine and agricultural economics, alongside the basic sciences, engineering and management.
299.c: The university is at Umudike, near Umuahia, in Abia State.

300.h: Modibbo Adama University, Yola is a federal university founded in 1981 as one of four federal universities of technology set up to advance science-based research and teaching. In 1984 it was merged into the University of Maiduguri as its Modibbo Adama campus. It regained its independence in 1988 as the Federal University of Technology, Yola, and was later renamed after Modibbo Adama, the founder of the Adamawa Emirate.
300.a: The university offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees as well as sub-degree programmes, and is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
300.c: Its campus is at Girei, near Yola, in Adamawa State, north-eastern Nigeria.

301.h: Mountain Top University (MTU) is a private Christian university founded in 2015 by Mountain of Fire and Miracles Ministries, the Pentecostal church founded by Daniel Kolawole Olukoya. It is known for strict rules and for the central place of spiritual activities in campus life.
301.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes in the sciences, humanities and management, and its music department is particularly well regarded.
301.c: The campus is at Makogi Oba in Ogun State, on the Lagos-Ibadan expressway.

303.h: Nasarawa State University, Keffi (NSUK) is a public university owned by the Nasarawa State Government. It was established under Nasarawa State Law No. 2 of 2001, passed during the administration of Governor Abdullahi Adamu, the state's first democratically elected governor, and began in February 2002 on the site of the former College of Arts, Science and Technology in Keffi.
303.a: The university was created to give students from Nasarawa State and its neighbours wider access to university education. It offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
303.c: The main campus is in Keffi, Nasarawa State, within easy reach of Abuja.

304.h: Niger Delta University (NDU) is a public university funded by the Bayelsa State Government. It was established in 2000 by Chief D. S. P. Alamieyeseigha, then governor of Bayelsa State.
304.a: NDU offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees and is a member of the Association of Commonwealth Universities. Its teaching hospital, Niger Delta University Teaching Hospital, is at Okolobiri.
304.c: The main campus is at Amassoma on Wilberforce Island, and the Faculty of Law is in Yenagoa, the state capital.

305.h: Nile University of Nigeria (NUN) is a private university established in 2009. It is part of the Honoris United Universities network and is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
305.a: The university has eight faculties and a School of Postgraduate Studies, offering 34 undergraduate and 47 postgraduate programmes. Its Centre for Lifelong Learning runs short professional courses.
305.c: The campus is in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

306.h: Nnamdi Azikiwe University (UNIZIK) is a federal university. It began as Anambra State University of Technology and was taken over by the Federal Government and renamed after Nnamdi Azikiwe, Nigeria's first president; the National Universities Commission records its establishment as a federal university in 1992.
306.a: UNIZIK is a large university offering undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in most disciplines, including medicine, which is taught at its Nnewi campus.
306.c: The main campus is in Awka, the capital of Anambra State, with a second major campus at Nnewi and further sites at Agulu and Ifite-Ogwari.

307.h: Novena University was the first private university in Delta State. It was founded in 2005, partly to meet demand from qualified students who could not find places at existing universities.
307.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes, supported by a library and student services.
307.c: It is located in Ogume, Delta State.

308.h: Oduduwa University is a private university established in 2009 and named after Oduduwa, regarded as the ancestor of the Yoruba people. It is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
308.c: It is located in Ipetumodu, near Ile-Ife, in Osun State.

309.h: Olabisi Onabanjo University (OOU) is a public university owned by the Ogun State Government. It was founded on 7 July 1982 as Ogun State University, and many people still call it OSU. On 29 May 2001 it was renamed after Olabisi Onabanjo, the civilian governor of Ogun State whose government established it.
309.a: OOU offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine.
309.c: The main campus is in Ago-Iwoye, Ogun State, and the university has several other campuses in the state.

311.h: Osun State University (UNIOSUN) is a public university owned by the Osun State Government. It was established under the administration of Prince Olagunsoye Oyinlola and approved by the National Universities Commission on 21 December 2006 as Nigeria's 30th state university and 80th university overall.
311.a: Each campus hosts particular faculties, for example health sciences at one and humanities and culture at another.
311.c: UNIOSUN is a multi-campus university, with six campuses spread across the state's six administrative zones: Osogbo, Ikire, Okuku, Ifetedo, Ipetu-Ijesha and Ejigbo.

312.h: PAMO University of Medical Sciences is a private university established in 2017 as the first private medical university in Nigeria. It was founded by Peter Odili, a medical doctor and former governor of Rivers State. Former head of state General Abdulsalami Abubakar was appointed chairman of its governing council and board of trustees in 2017.
312.a: The university specialises in medicine and the health sciences.
312.c: It is located at Iriebe, near Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

313.h: Pan-Atlantic University (PAU) is a private, non-profit university. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2002. It grew out of the Lagos Business School, which remains its best-known school.
313.a: PAU is known for business and management education through the Lagos Business School, and also offers programmes in media and communication, the sciences and other fields.
313.c: The main campus is in Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos State.

314.h: Paul University, Awka (PUA) is a private Christian university founded in 2009 by the bishops of the five Anglican ecclesiastical provinces east of the Niger. It replaced St Paul's University College, which the Church Missionary Society founded in 1904 to train church workers.
314.a: The university offers undergraduate degrees in arts, natural and applied sciences, social sciences and management. It is fully residential and was planned to grow from about 400 students towards 3,500.
314.c: It is located in Awka, the capital of Anambra State.

315.h: Philomath University is a private multidisciplinary university established in 2021.
315.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
315.c: It is located in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

316.h: Plateau State University (PLASU) is a public university owned by the Plateau State Government. It was established under Plateau State Law No. 4 of 7 March 2005 and recognised by the National Universities Commission on 29 April 2005 as Nigeria's 66th university and 24th state university.
316.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
316.c: The campus is in Diram village, on the Butura-Tarangol road in Bokkos local government area, about 70 kilometres from Jos, the state capital.

317.h: Precious Cornerstone University is a private university founded in 2017 by the Sword of the Spirit Ministries, a Pentecostal church in Ibadan led by Bishop Francis Wale Oke. It held its first matriculation in 2019, admitting 78 pioneer students.
317.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
317.c: It is located in Ibadan, Oyo State.

318.h: Redeemer's University (RUN) is a private university established in 2005 and owned by the Redeemed Christian Church of God. It moved from its first site near Lagos to a permanent campus in Ede.
318.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in the sciences, humanities, social sciences, law and engineering.
318.c: The campus is in Ede, Osun State, off the Ibadan-Osogbo road.

319.h: Renaissance University is a private university licensed by the Federal Government in 2005.
319.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
319.c: Its main campus is at Ugbawka in Enugu State.

320.h: Rhema University, Aba is a private Christian university founded by Living Word Ministries International. The church set up a planning committee for the university in 2004, and it received its licence from the National Universities Commission and admitted its first students in 2009.
320.c: It is located in Aba, the commercial city of Abia State.

321.h: Ritman University is a private university founded by Emmanuel Ibok Essien, who represented Akwa Ibom North-West in the Nigerian Senate from 1999 to 2003. The National Universities Commission granted its operating licence on 5 March 2015, and teaching began on 23 November 2015.
321.a: The university offers a range of undergraduate programmes.
321.c: It is located in Ikot Ekpene, Akwa Ibom State.

322.h: Salem University is a private university. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2007.
322.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and provides academic advisers to support students.
322.c: It is located in Lokoja, the capital of Kogi State, and offers on-campus hostel accommodation.
